question: Prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI from cognitive scores plus MRI measures. P-178 studies early-MCI patients with eventual conversion (mean 5.02 years), using clinical scales plus hippocampal and ventricular volume. P-183 studies MCI patients aged 70-80, progressing to AD at 2 years against stable for at least 5 years, using neuropsychological scores plus T2-map signal and texture features. The rule allows these differences in population subset, horizon and features.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy and AUC with AUC. The record's 'P-183: Acc 72.7' is not a P-183 accuracy: 0.727 is the neuropsychology-only LASSO AUC. P-183's printed accuracies are used instead (best 0.775), under condition 6.

figures.P-178: 9-feature random forest, visit-level records, 95 test patients (about 12 converters). Accuracy 0.936, Wilson with n = 95: centre (0.936 + 0.0202)/1.0404 = 0.919, half-width 0.051 -> 0.868-0.970. AUC 0.96, Hanley-McNeil with 12/83: Q1 = 0.923, Q2 = 0.940, SE = sqrt([0.0384 + 11(0.0015) + 82(0.0188)]/996) = 0.040 -> 0.882-1.000. Class-wise figures follow from Table 4. The majority-class SVC scores accuracy = precision = 0.900 with recall 1, so the test set is 90% non-converters and precision and recall refer to that class. For the RF, recall 0.978 and precision 0.952 give non-converters correct 0.9(0.978) = 0.880, predicted non-converters 0.880/0.952 = 0.925, converters missed 0.044 and converters found 0.056. That is converter sensitivity 0.556 and specificity 0.978, which reproduces the accuracy of 0.936 and gives a balanced accuracy of 0.767 (subject-level SE about 0.072 -> 0.626-0.908).
figures.P-183: Imaging plus neuropsychology, 40 subjects (18 progressors/22 stable), 100 random 80/20 splits, 95% CIs as printed. RF: accuracy 0.775 (0.615-0.892), sensitivity 0.722, specificity 0.818 (balanced 0.770), AUC 0.770 (0.636-0.905). BSWiMS: accuracy 0.775 (0.615-0.892), sensitivity 0.778, specificity 0.773, balanced error 0.223 (0.100-0.359), i.e. balanced accuracy 0.777 (0.641-0.900). ENS: AUC 0.824 (0.681-0.968), the best AUC.
figures.comparison: Raw accuracy: 0.936 lies above 0.892 and 0.775 below 0.868, so each lies outside the other's interval. Prevalence-adjusted: P-178's class-wise figures at P-183's 45% converters give 0.45(0.556) + 0.55(0.978) = 0.788, inside P-183's 0.615-0.892, and the balanced accuracies are 0.767 against 0.770 and 0.777. AUC: P-183's best, 0.824, lies below P-178's derived lower bound of 0.882. P-178's 0.96 lies inside P-183's ENS interval (upper bound 0.968) but outside its RF interval (0.905). Against P-183's best model, the AUC exclusion runs one way.

matched_figure_check: Neither paper reports a result under the other's condition. P-178 has no fixed 2-year horizon and no near-balanced test, and P-183 has no early-MCI or eventual-conversion subset. P-178's own printed precision and recall, with the test prevalence that its SVC row fixes at 90% non-converters, reconstruct its classifier's sensitivity (0.556) and specificity (0.978). At P-183's class ratio these give 0.788, inside P-183's interval. So the accuracy gap in the record is produced by P-178's 90%-majority test set, and P-178's own figures dissolve it. The AUC gap does not depend on prevalence, and no figure in either paper reconciles it.
performance_validity: Passes as written: P-178's 0.936 and 0.96 are below 0.97 on 383 patients, and P-183's figures are far below. P-178's design is optimistic in ways that are candidate explanations rather than the exclusion. It uses visit-level records with random minority oversampling. Its Table 1 lists oversampled testing records (402/402) although the test set its SVC row implies is 90% non-converters. It chose its feature group by test accuracy. P-183's 40-subject sample makes its intervals wide.

candidate_explanations.difference: Class prevalence (accuracy only): P-178's test set is 90% non-converters and P-183's is near-balanced. P-178's own figures show this is enough to explain the accuracy gap, but it does not bear on AUC.

the inclusion criteria forced us to work with a small population

reason: On AUC the pair meets all six conditions, as C-121 does: the same question and channels, P-183's best AUC (0.824) below P-178's derived interval (0.882-1.000), no matched figure, and nothing near ceiling. But the disagreement the record rests on, accuracy, is dissolved by P-178's own printed precision and recall. At P-183's class ratio P-178's classifier would score 0.788, inside P-183's interval, and the balanced accuracies are 0.767 against 0.770-0.777. The AUC exclusion also runs one way only, since P-178's 0.96 lies inside P-183's 0.681-0.968. Whether to report the pair therefore rests on the AUC alone and is the operator's call, as in C-77. The candidate explanations for the AUC gap are not shown to be sufficient.
